To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
academic intellectual property interests and Pharma quality criteria for medicinal chemistry are in opposition.
intellectual property considerations decrease research output in subtle and un-anticipated ways.

academic and Pharma medicinal chemist views of chemical quality are very different and that this difference is a major obstacle to the exchange of chemical probe information between academia and Pharma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the current intellectual property environment on the productivity of research.
the effects of intellectual property considerations on research productivity and on academic/Pharma collaboration.
the impact of IP considerations on the development of novel medicines and the development of the academic/ Pharma partnership.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
academic intellectual property interests have a detrimental effect on the quality and quantity of academic research and on Pharma research.
intellectual property considerations have had a negative influence on the development and application of chemical biology.
intellectual property interests in the academic domain have a detrimental effect on research productivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anti-intellectual effect of intellectual property on research productivity is subtle and pervasive.
academic intellectual property considerations have an unanticipated anti-intellectual effect on research productivity and the ability of Pharma to access the academic drug target space.
intellectual property is an impediment to the progress of science.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the academic and Pharma medicinal chemistry domains are not as well aligned as one would like.
intellectual property considerations can have anti-intellectual consequences.
intellectual property considerations are a subtle but significant impediment to academic/industry collaboration in chemical probe exchange.
